 7                SENATOR LaVALLE:   Mr. President, 

 8   with unanimous consent I'd like to recognize 

 9   Senator Espaillat for a brief announcement.

10                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:    

11   Without objection, Senator Espaillat, you are 

12   recognized.

13                SENATOR ESPAILLAT:   Thank you, 

14   Mr. President.  

15                Thank you for allowing me to 

16   introduce a group that has been coming to the 

17   New York State Legislature since February of 

18   1997.  They are the Instituto Duartiano.  They 

19   celebrate the anniversary of the birth of Juan 

20   Pablo Duarte, the founding father of the 

21   Dominican Republic, who was born the 26th of 

22   January of 1813.  

23                There's a big delegation this 

24   year, headed by the president of the institute, 

25   Mr. Juan Elliott, and representatives from the 

                                                                246

 1   Dominican Republic Consul General's office.  

 2   The consul general, Mr. Maximo Corcino, could 

 3   not be here today, but he sent Isabel Padilla, 

 4   who's head of the delegation, along with 

 5   Cecilia Baez, who are both in the balcony.  

 6                And they're celebrating, they're 

 7   kicking off Juan Pablo Duarte week, and it has 

 8   been a tradition of this group to visit both 

 9   the Assembly and the Senate and visit the 

10   proceedings.  So I thank you, Mr. President, 

11   for allowing me to introduce them and to make 

12   sure that the entire Senate understands what 

13   they're about.  They're about the legacy of 

14   Juan Pablo Duarte, particularly for young 

15   children, teaching them who he was.  And 

16   they're doing a fantastic job.  

17                So thank you for allowing them to 

18   visit the Senate chambers.

22   Mr. President.  

23                I also stand to welcome our guests 

24   today to the Senate chamber.  And there's a 

25   couple of reasons why I do that.  And the most

 1   important one is because I represent about 

 2   100,000 Dominicans in my district.  Many of 

 3   them have actually crossed over from Washington 

 4   Heights -- Quisqueya Heights, if you will -- 

 5   where many have lived for generations.  

 6                And I increasingly find that 

 7   there's many of these folks that are in my back 

 8   yard.  They are my allies locally.  In here in 

 9   the Senate I obviously have two colleagues, 

10   Adriano Espaillat and Jose Peralta, which are 

11   both Dominican.  And I would be remiss if I did 

12   not mention my colleague in the Assembly, 

13   Nelson Castro, who crosses over with me in the 

14   district.

15                This is a community that is a rich 

16   community.  It is a community that is rich with 

17   culture.  They are a zesty community.  They 

18   enjoy participating in politics; to them, it is 

19   a full-contact sport.  And I enjoy having them 

20   as my colleagues here in the Senate, colleagues 

21   in the Assembly, but most importantly as people 

22   that I represent in my district.  

23                Thank you again for coming today.  

24   Bienvenidos a senado {in Spanish}.  And I hope 

25   that all of my colleagues take some time to 

                                                                248

 1   also welcome them as well.

 7                SENATOR PERKINS:   Bienvenidos.  I 

 8   am a Senator of the Dominican community {in 

 9   Spanish}.  Entiende?  Gracias.  

10                It's a great pleasure that I have 

11   to serve as a Senator that represents part of 

12   the Dominican community.  As a community I've 

13   had the privilege of working with them for 

14   many, many years.  

15                Long before he was a great state 

16   Senator, I remember working with Senator 

17   Espaillat when he actually was a candidate for 

18   a very local position as a member of the 

19   community school board.  It was a very historic 

20   period because then, in our recognition of the 

21   value of immigrants and the value of parents, 

22   we allowed them to vote in school board 

23   elections.  And he was a great organizer of the 

24   Dominican community in Manhattan to get them 

25   out to participate in the electoral process.  

                                                                249

 1   And now they have become a political giant, not 

 2   only in Manhattan but in the whole City of New 

 3   York.  

 4                And so I want to thank you for the 

 5   privilege of being here with you and the 

 6   opportunity to work with your brother from the 

 7   Dominican Republic.  Welcome.

 8                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 9   Diaz.

10                SENATOR DIAZ:   Thank you, 

11   Mr. President.

12                Ladies and gentlemen, as you know, 

13   every country has their heroes and heroines, 

14   and most of them have specific days in which to 

15   honor their heroes.  For example, Africa honors 

16   Nelson Mandela, America honors George 

17   Washington, Abraham Lincoln, Martin Luther 

18   King, and many others.  Puerto Rico honors Don 

19   Luis Munoz Marin and Don Pedro Albizu Campus, 

20   among others.  

21                The Dominican Republic honors the 

22   birth of Juan Pablo Duarte y Diez, born on 

23   July 26, 1813, and who died on July 15, 1876.  

24   In his 63 years of life, Juan Pablo Duarte y 

25   Diez left a legacy of pride, courage, and honor 

                                                                250

 1   for all Dominicans to celebrate.  

 2                Together with Don Francisco del 

 3   Rosario and Ramon Matias Mella, Juan Pablo 

 4   Duarte y Diez was a visionary who is widely 

 5   considered as the architect of the Dominican 

 6   Republic and its independence from Haiti in 

 7   1844.  

 8                That is why, Mr. President and 

 9   ladies and gentlemen, today I'm proud to honor 

10   my colleague and friend, my brother Adriano 

11   Espaillat, in congratulating the people of the 

12   Dominican Republic on this occasion and 

13   supporting this wonderful resolution declaring 

14   January 23rd Juan Pablo Duarte Day in the State 

15   of New York. 

16                To Mr. Juan Elliott, president of 

17   the Instituto Duartiano, and the delegation 

18   from New York City that are here visiting us 

19   today, congratulations and thank you all for 

20   honoring us with your presence.  

21                And to you {singing}:  

22                "Quisqueyanos valiantes, alcemos,     

23                Nuestro canto con viva emoción."  

24   Hey -- {in Spanish}.  Muchos gracias.
